paper.citation: Maharana et al., Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents, ACL 2024
paper.metric: token F1 on gold answers (not LLM-as-judge)

llm_judge_accuracy.note: Public locomo10 leaderboards use an answer LLM plus a judge LLM. Protocols differ: judge model, top-k, whether adversarial items are dropped, partial credit. Published overall scores commonly fall around 67–80 when adversarial is excluded; some re-runs exceed 90 with a stronger judge or a different harness. Do not treat those as paper F1.

retrieval_recall.note: Whether gold evidence appears in the retrieved set. Strong hybrid systems report R@5 in the low-to-mid 90s. That is not end-to-end QA accuracy.

memlayer_scorecard.smoke: BM25 plus lexical contain on a one-query fixture. Wiring check only; not a LoCoMo score.
memlayer_scorecard.full: Ingest locomo10.json, hybrid-rerank retrieval, LLM answer plus LLM judge. accuracy_pct is the judge pass rate. Scorecard 2.0 reports recall_at_k and MRR as retrieval metrics; token-F1 is not emitted.

how_to_beat_or_compare: Smoke (`make eval-locomo-smoke`) only proves the CLI harness. Never quote it against published numbers.
Full (`make eval-locomo`) is the local analysis run. Optional LIMIT=N for a cheaper slice.
Compare accuracy_pct only to other LLM-judge locomo10 runs that disclose judge model, k, and whether adversarial questions are included.
To beat paper F1 (51.6 overall / 87.9 human), you need token-overlap F1 on gold answers. memlayer does not emit that metric.
Use recall_at_k / MRR to diagnose retrieval; they are independent of the judge.

To land in the published LLM-judge band (~67–80+), use the default LoCoMo profile (hybrid + rerank + evidence window), ingest speaker-prefixed turns, keep fact fusion on, and use a capable answer/judge model. Match the other system's category filter.
Retrieval R@k is the right metric if you only care whether evidence was fetched; it will look stronger than judged QA.
